Title: Diagnosis
Details: The corresponding issue report describes that tooltip text in the UI is displayed with HTML entities such as " instead of the intended characters. This strongly suggests a missing escaping or decoding step in tooltip generation. Inspecting the implementation of StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment reveals that it directly returns the toolTipText without applying any escaping. Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

After providing this diagnosis, you will be prompted to suggest which methods would be the best locations to be fixed. The answers should be in the form of `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` without commentary (one per line), as your answer will be automatically processed before finally being presented to the user.

messages.content:
Title: Diagnosis
Details: The issue arises because the test uses a supplementary character (a Unicode code point outside the Basic Multilingual Plane, composed of a surrogate pair in UTF-16). The test expects that escapeXml returns the input unchanged because the input string doesn't contain characters that need XML escaping. 

The code of StringEscapeUtils.escapeXml simply delegates to ESCAPE_XML.translate. The ESCAPE_XML field is an AggregateTranslator holding two LookupTranslator instances, each configured with a lookup table for common XML escapes.

The CharSequenceTranslator.translate method processes the input string by code points, but the LookupTranslator.translate method operates on CharSequence substrings using indices and lengths based on char counts, not Unicode code points. When the translate method in LookupTranslator tries to get substrings from the input, it may misinterpret surrogate pairs due to incorrect length/index calculations, especially at the boundary of surrogate pairs (code points in supplementary planes).

The Loop in CharSequenceTranslator translates code points by incrementing position using codePointCount etc., but the LookupTranslator accesses input.subSequence(index, index + i) where index and i are char indices, not code point indices. Inconsistency in handling surrogate pairs leads to wrong results when input includes supplementary plane characters.

This mismatch explains why escapeXml outputs wrong results: the LookupTranslator misinterprets surrogate pairs and transforms or alters them incorrectly. Since the input contains supplementary characters (surrogate pairs) and "A", and none require escaping, the output should be identical but isn't.

Hence, the root cause is LookupTranslator.translate operates on char indices incorrectly on surrogate pairs, resulting in wrong substring extraction and subsequent translation for supplementary characters.

Next, it is appropriate to check the interplay of index and position counting and how surrogate pairs are handled during lookup in LookupTranslator.translate to confirm the bug.
